sentences.text: Revenue moved from $41.9 billion in FY2016 to $47.9 billion in FY2025, a 1.5% CAGR [F1][F10][F219].
The path was not smooth: revenue fell 13.5% in FY2017 and 5.3% in FY2018, then recovered 17.1% in FY2021 and 11.3% in FY2022 [D42][D93][D246][D297].
The FY2017 decline came with refranchising of bottling operations, which cut operating cash flow by 20% that year [F92][D47][P75].
Operating margin set its window low of 20.7% in FY2016 and its high of 28.7% in FY2025, against a 26.0% median [F41][F50][D764][D765][D766].
Concentrate operations supplied 59.4% of FY2025 revenue and 1.6pp of its 1.9% growth, while finished product operations added 0.3pp [D532][D534][D449][D541].
North America was the largest segment at 40.9% of revenue, contributing 1.5pp of FY2025 growth [D611][D613].
Worldwide concentrate sales volume grew 1% in FY2025 while unit case volume was even [P16].
Operating income grew 37.7% against 1.9% revenue growth, and revenue growth exceeded operating-cost growth by 9.7pp [D450][D449][D474].
Diluted EPS grew 23.6% against 23.3% net income growth, with the diluted share count down 0.2% [D453][D451][D468].
FY2025 operating margin of 28.7% sits 2.7pp above the 26.0% window median and at the window high [F50][D766][D765].

The 7.5pp operating-margin gain came mainly from lower other operating charges after the prior-year fairlife contingent-consideration remeasurement, plus concentrate volume growth and pricing [D463][P12].
Cost of revenue added 0.6pp and SG&A 0.7pp, while the residual other lines added 6.2pp [D475][D476][D477].
Gross margin rose 0.6pp to 61.6% on favorable pricing and prior-year refranchising, partly offset by currency and higher commodity costs [F30][D462][P14].
Net margin of 27.3% ran 1.4pp below operating margin, with a 17.9% effective tax rate [F70][D810][D435].
Operating cash flow of $7.4 billion was 0.57x net income in FY2025, the window low against a 1.18x median [F100][D436][D799][D800].
Free cash flow of $5.3 billion was 0.40x net income and an 11.0% margin, versus a 20.2% median margin [F120][D437][D433][D775].

FY2024 operating cash flow fell 41.3% on a $6.0 billion IRS tax litigation deposit and refranchising, and FY2025's 8.9% rise came from lower tax payments and working-capital timing [D404][F100][D454][P22][P1].
Capex of $2.1 billion was 4.4% of revenue and 2.01x D&A [F110][D432][D438].
Cash and equivalents were $10.3 billion at FY2025, down 5.2% [F160][D458].
Net debt was $32.4 billion at FY2023, or 70.7% of revenue, but long-term debt is not reported after FY2023 so later net cash is not comparable [D341][D342][X194].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.5 billion were 179.9% of free cash flow in FY2025, and repurchases fell to $746 million from $3.7 billion in FY2016 [D444][D445][X135][X126].
Return on average equity was 46.0%, above the 36.5% peer median, at the 67th percentile of six peers [D448][D798][D797].

Revenue for FY2017 and FY2018 is a later recast, $36.2 billion and $34.3 billion versus $35.4 billion and $31.9 billion first reported, so growth across those years mixes presentations [F2][X2][F3][X3][R1].
Long-term debt stops after FY2023, so total debt, net cash and the net-cash peer rank omit it from FY2024 onward [X194][R9].
Cash and investments omit an unmapped short-term investment line, understating the total by $3.6 billion in FY2025 [F160][D440][R11].
Free cash flow has run below 80% of net income for two years, at 0.45x in FY2024 and 0.40x in FY2025 [D387][D437][R3].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, reaching 214.2% in FY2024 [D344][D395][D445][R2].
If operating cash flow stays below the 1.18x net-income median, the cash-conversion break persists; a return above it would reverse the trend [D800][D436].
Operating margin at the 28.7% window high is the level to hold; a fall toward the 26.0% median would mark the FY2025 gain as one-off [F50][D765][D766].
Buybacks plus dividends at 179.9% of free cash flow need free cash flow to recover toward the 20.2% margin median to be covered [D445][D775].
